---
title: "Severe Crises. Silent Headlines."
subtitle: Tracking where suffering is high and global attention is low
description: "A monthly SA Analytical dashboard showing humanitarian and development indicators side by side for each sector, using established international classifications, with climate vulnerability, media attention and funding."
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    scrolling: true
    theme: [darkly, brand.scss]
    logo: logo.png
    embed-resources: true
output-file: index.html
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)
library(reactable)
library(readr)

# ---- Brand ---------------------------------------------------------------
anthracite <- "#2B2B2E"
card_grey  <- "#36363A"
deep_grey  <- "#1F1F21"
line_grey  <- "#45454A"
gold       <- "#AF8B2F"   # GOLD: website uses #B5943F
gold_light <- "#C9AA58"
gold_pale  <- "#F0D48A"
text_light <- "#E8E6E1"
trend_colours <- c("#FFF1C4", gold, text_light, "#E0BE62", "#8C8C92", gold_light, "#B8B0A4", "#7A6328")
trend_dashes  <- c("solid", "solid", "dash", "dash", "dot", "dot", "dashdot", "dashdot")

chart_font <- list(color = text_light, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif")
dark_axis  <- list(gridcolor = line_grey, zerolinecolor = line_grey,
                   linecolor = line_grey, tickfont = chart_font)

# ---- Map colours -----------------------------------------------------------
# Vulnerability / severity: 10 bands, green (0, no vulnerability) -> dark red (10, highest)
sev_colours <- c("#E8F5DF", "#D2EDBC", "#C5E4A0", "#D6DC84", "#E6CC66",
                 "#E6AE48", "#E08A2E", "#C9581F", "#A02C16", "#6E0B0B")
sev_scale <- do.call(c, lapply(seq_along(sev_colours), function(i)
  list(c((i - 1) / 10, sev_colours[i]), c(i / 10, sev_colours[i]))))
ocean_blue  <- "#00022E"   
grid_blue   <- "#3A6A94"
nodata_grey <- "#8A8A8F"

flat_geo <- list(bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", showframe = FALSE,
                 showcoastlines = TRUE, coastlinecolor = "#FFFFFF" , coastlinewidth = 1,
                 showocean = TRUE, oceancolor = ocean_blue,
                 showlakes = TRUE, lakecolor = ocean_blue,
                 showland = TRUE, landcolor = nodata_grey,
                 showcountries = TRUE, countrycolor = "#FFFFFF",
                 projection = list(type = "natural earth"))

cbar <- function(title) {
  list(title = list(text = title, side = "top", font = chart_font),
       tickfont = chart_font, outlinewidth = 0, thickness = 20, len = 0.6, dtick = 1,
       x = 0.97, xanchor = "left", y = 0.5, yanchor = "middle")
}

# Grey "no data" key, placed just below the colour bar
nodata_key <- function(text = "No data", font = list(color = text_light, size = 11, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif")) {
  list(text = paste0("<span style='color:", nodata_grey, "'>\u25A0</span> ", text),
       x = 0.97, y = 0.15, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
       xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top", showarrow = FALSE, align = "left",
       font = font)
}

# ---- SA Analytical brand style for the global vulnerability map -------------
brand_gold       <- "#b5943f"   # accent: menu, labels, lines
brand_gold_light <- "#c9aa58"   # accent hover
brand_charcoal   <- "#2b2b2e"   # dark band
brand_text       <- "#e7dfd2"   # text on dark bands
brand_text_soft  <- "#f5efe6"   # light text on dark (hover boxes)
brand_on_gold    <- "#1a1a1b"   # text on gold

brand_font_small <- list(color = brand_text, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 11)
brand_hover <- list(bgcolor = brand_charcoal, bordercolor = brand_gold,
                    font = list(color = brand_text_soft, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 12))

# Colour bar: title as a gold eyebrow label (DM Sans, uppercase), ticks in brand text colour
cbar_brand <- function(title) {
  list(title = list(text = title, side = "top",
                    font = list(color = brand_gold, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 10)),
       tickfont = brand_font_small, outlinewidth = 0, thickness = 20, len = 0.6, dtick = 1,
       x = 0.97, xanchor = "left", y = 0.5, yanchor = "middle")
}

sa_table_theme <- reactableTheme(
  color = text_light, backgroundColor = card_grey,
  borderColor = line_grey, highlightColor = line_grey,
  style = list(fontFamily = "DM Sans, sans-serif"),
  headerStyle = list(background = deep_grey, color = gold, textTransform = "uppercase",
                     letterSpacing = "0.1em", fontSize = "0.72rem", fontWeight = 500),
  searchInputStyle = list(backgroundColor = deep_grey, color = text_light, borderColor = line_grey)
)

value_style <- "font-family: Syne, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.7rem;"

# Dates written in English whatever the computer's language
month_label <- function(ym) paste(month.name[as.integer(substr(ym, 6, 7))], substr(ym, 1, 4))
date_label  <- function(d) paste(as.integer(format(d, "%d")),
                                 month.abb[as.integer(format(d, "%m"))], format(d, "%Y"))
this_year <- as.numeric(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))

# ===========================================================================
# ATTENTION & FUNDING (neglect tracker)
# ===========================================================================

# ---- Severity (ACAPS INFORM): decides the countries AND the month ------
severity <- read_csv("data/severity.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
im <- unique(severity$inform_month)
if (length(im) != 1) stop("severity.csv contains more than one INFORM month. Re-run 03_inform.R.")
ref_month <- sprintf("%s-%02d", substr(im, 4, 7), match(substr(im, 1, 3), month.abb))
ref_label <- month_label(ref_month)

# ---- News attention (GDELT): locked to the INFORM month ----------------
attention_all <- read_csv("data/attention_monthly.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
if (!ref_month %in% attention_all$month) {
  stop("GDELT has no data for ", ref_label, ", the INFORM month. ",
       "Re-run the scripts so both sources cover the same month.")
}
attention <- attention_all |>
  filter(month == ref_month) |>
  select(iso3, attention = share_per_10k)

# ---- Funding (OCHA FTS): year-to-date ----------------------------------
funding_raw  <- read_csv("data/funding.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
funding_date <- if ("as_of" %in% names(funding_raw)) max(funding_raw$as_of) else
                  as.Date(file.info("data/funding.csv")$mtime)
funding <- select(funding_raw, iso3, funded_pct)

# ---- Combine -----------------------------------------------------------
neglect <- severity |>
  select(iso3, country, severity, top_crisis, crises) |>
  left_join(attention, by = "iso3") |>
  left_join(funding,   by = "iso3")

scatter_data <- neglect |>
  filter(!is.na(attention)) |>
  mutate(gap   = severity - log1p(attention),
         label = ifelse(rank(-severity, ties.method = "first") <= 8, country, ""),
         dot   = ifelse(label != "", gold_pale, gold))

top <- scatter_data |> arrange(desc(gap))

trend_iso <- neglect |> filter(!is.na(attention)) |>
  arrange(desc(severity)) |> slice_head(n = 8) |> pull(iso3)
trend_data <- attention_all |>
  filter(iso3 %in% trend_iso, month <= ref_month) |>
  select(iso3, month, share_per_10k) |>
  left_join(select(neglect, iso3, name = country), by = "iso3") |>
  arrange(month) |>
  mutate(month_lab = paste0(month.abb[as.integer(substr(month, 6, 7))], "-", substr(month, 3, 4)),
         month_lab = factor(month_lab, levels = unique(month_lab)))

# ===========================================================================
# SECTOR DATA: established indicators only (no SA Analytical scoring)
# ===========================================================================

read_opt <- function(f, empty) if (file.exists(f)) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) else empty

structural <- read_csv("data/structural.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ind <- function(cd) structural |> filter(code == cd) |> select(iso3, value, year)

ipc   <- read_opt("data/ipc.csv",   tibble(iso3 = character(), ipc3_pct = numeric(),
                                           ipc3_people = numeric(), ipc_to = as.Date(character())))
needs <- read_opt("data/needs.csv", tibble(iso3 = character(), sector = character(),
                                           ref_end = as.Date(character()), pin = numeric()))
climate_detail <- read_opt("data/climate_detail.csv",
                           tibble(iso3 = character(), measure = character(), score = numeric(), year = integer()))

pop <- ind("SP.POP.TOTL") |> select(iso3, pop = value)

country_names <- bind_rows(distinct(structural, iso3, country),
                           select(severity, iso3, country)) |>
  distinct(iso3, .keep_all = TRUE)

# People in need as a share of the population (from humanitarian needs overviews)
pin_of <- function(sec) {
  needs |>
    filter(sector == sec) |>
    left_join(pop, by = "iso3") |>
    filter(!is.na(pop), pop > 0) |>
    transmute(iso3, value = pmin(100, 100 * pin / pop), pin, year = as.integer(format(ref_end, "%Y")))
}

ipc_d <- ipc |> transmute(iso3, value = ipc3_pct, people = ipc3_people,
                          year = as.integer(format(as.Date(ipc_to), "%Y")))

# WHO/UNICEF prevalence thresholds (de Onis et al., 2019)
who_labels    <- c("Very low", "Low", "Medium", "High", "Very high")
stunting_cuts <- c(2.5, 10, 20, 30)   # % of children under 5
wasting_cuts  <- c(2.5, 5, 10, 15)
who_class <- function(x, cuts) findInterval(x, cuts) + 1   # 1 = very low ... 5 = very high

# ---- Map helpers --------------------------------------------------------------
smooth_scale <- lapply(seq_along(sev_colours), function(i)
  c((i - 1) / (length(sev_colours) - 1), sev_colours[i]))
class_cols  <- sev_colours[c(1, 3, 5, 8, 10)]
class_scale <- do.call(c, lapply(1:5, function(i)
  list(c((i - 1) / 5, class_cols[i]), c(i / 5, class_cols[i]))))

# "Get the data" link in the top-right corner of a map; opens that tab's section of the Data page
# in a new browser tab. Plotly only accepts full web addresses (https://...) in links.
data_page <- "https://dashboard.sa-analytical.com/data.html"
data_link <- function(section) {
  list(text = paste0("<a href='", data_page, "#", section, "' target='_blank' style='color:", brand_gold, "'>",
                     "Get the data \u2192</a>"),
       x = 1, y = 1, xref = "paper", yref = "paper", xanchor = "right", yanchor = "bottom",
       showarrow = FALSE, font = list(color = brand_gold, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 12))
}

map_layout <- function(p, key_text, caption, section) {
  p |>
    layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", dragmode = FALSE,
           font = list(color = brand_text, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif"),
           hoverlabel = brand_hover, geo = flat_geo,
           margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 22, b = 30),
           annotations = list(
             data_link(section),
             nodata_key(key_text, font = brand_font_small),
             list(text = caption, x = 0.01, y = 0, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
                  xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top", showarrow = FALSE, align = "left",
                  font = list(color = "#8a8278", family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 10)))) |>
    config(displayModeBar = FALSE, scrollZoom = FALSE)
}

add_names <- function(d) d |> left_join(country_names, by = "iso3") |> filter(!is.na(country))

# Continuous map of a percentage. reverse = TRUE when higher values are better.
pct_map <- function(d, label, bar_title, key_text, caption, section, zmax = 100, reverse = FALSE) {
  d <- add_names(d) |>
    mutate(hover = paste0("<b>", country, "</b><br>", label, ": ",
                          sprintf("%.1f", value), "%", " (", year, ")"))
  plot_ly(d, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~value, zmin = 0, zmax = zmax,
          colorscale = smooth_scale, reversescale = reverse, text = ~hover,
          hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
          colorbar = list(title = list(text = bar_title, side = "top",
                                       font = list(color = brand_gold, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 10)),
                          tickfont = brand_font_small, ticksuffix = "%", outlinewidth = 0,
                          thickness = 20, len = 0.6, x = 0.97, xanchor = "left", y = 0.5, yanchor = "middle"),
          marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
    map_layout(key_text, caption, section)
}

# Map of an established five-class classification (e.g. WHO prevalence thresholds)
class_map <- function(d, cuts, label, bar_title, key_text, caption, section) {
  d <- add_names(d) |>
    mutate(cls = who_class(value, cuts),
           hover = paste0("<b>", country, "</b><br>", label, ": ", sprintf("%.1f", value), "%",
                          " (", year, ")<br>Classification: ", who_labels[cls]))
  plot_ly(d, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~cls, zmin = 0.5, zmax = 5.5,
          colorscale = class_scale, text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
          colorbar = list(title = list(text = bar_title, side = "top",
                                       font = list(color = brand_gold, family = "DM Sans, sans-serif", size = 10)),
                          tickvals = 1:5, ticktext = who_labels, tickfont = brand_font_small,
                          outlinewidth = 0, thickness = 20, len = 0.6,
                          x = 0.97, xanchor = "left", y = 0.5, yanchor = "middle"),
          marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
    map_layout(key_text, caption, section)
}

# ---- Global tab: INFORM Risk (JRC), Development & Deprivation component -------
inform_risk <- read_opt("data/inform_risk.csv",
                        tibble(iso3 = character(), risk = numeric(), vulnerability = numeric(),
                               lcc = numeric(), dev_depr = numeric(), release = character()))
risk_release <- if (nrow(inform_risk) > 0) as.character(inform_risk$release[1]) else "(not loaded)"

dev_global <- inform_risk |>
  filter(!is.na(dev_depr)) |>
  add_names() |>
  mutate(hover = paste0("<b>", country, "</b>",
                        "<br>Development & deprivation: ", sprintf("%.1f", dev_depr),
                        ifelse(is.na(lcc), "", paste0("<br>Lack of coping capacity: ", sprintf("%.1f", lcc))),
                        ifelse(is.na(risk), "", paste0("<br>INFORM Risk (overall): ", sprintf("%.1f", risk))),
                        "<br>INFORM Risk ", risk_release))

hum_global <- severity |>
  transmute(iso3, country, value = severity, top_crisis,
            hover = paste0("<b>", country, "</b><br>Crisis severity: ", sprintf("%.1f", severity),
                           "<br>", top_crisis))
```

# Global vulnerability map

## Row {height=600px}

```{r}
#| title: "Humanitarian: crisis severity"
plot_ly(hum_global, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~value, zmin = 0, zmax = 10,
        colorscale = sev_scale, text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
        colorbar = cbar_brand("CRISIS<br>SEVERITY"),
        marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
  map_layout("Not assessed",
             paste0("ACAPS INFORM Severity Index (0-10), ", ref_label, ". Grey: no crisis assessed by ACAPS."),
             "global")
```

```{r}
#| title: "Development: development & deprivation (INFORM Risk)"
plot_ly(dev_global, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~dev_depr, zmin = 0, zmax = 10,
        colorscale = sev_scale, text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
        colorbar = cbar_brand("DEVELOPMENT &<br>DEPRIVATION"),
        marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
  map_layout("No data",
             paste0("INFORM Risk ", risk_release, ", European Commission JRC (CC BY 4.0). ",
                    "Development & deprivation component (0-10), shown as published."),
             "global")
```

# Climate

## Row {height=600px}

```{r}
#| title: "Climate vulnerability (ND-GAIN)"
clim_v <- climate_detail |> filter(measure == "vulnerability") |>
  transmute(iso3, value = score, year) |> add_names() |>
  left_join(climate_detail |> filter(measure == "readiness") |> select(iso3, lack_ready = score), by = "iso3") |>
  mutate(hover = paste0("<b>", country, "</b><br>Climate vulnerability: ", sprintf("%.1f", value),
                        ifelse(is.na(lack_ready), "",
                               paste0("<br>Lack of readiness to adapt: ", sprintf("%.1f", lack_ready))),
                        "<br>ND-GAIN data year: ", year))
plot_ly(clim_v, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~value, zmin = 0, zmax = 10,
        colorscale = sev_scale, text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
        colorbar = cbar_brand("CLIMATE<br>VULNERABILITY"),
        marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
  map_layout("No data", "ND-GAIN vulnerability (0-1, shown x10): exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity.",
             "climate")
```

## Row {height=480px}

```{r}
#| title: "Crisis severity map"
plot_ly(neglect, type = "choropleth", locations = ~iso3, z = ~severity,
        zmin = 0, zmax = 10, colorscale = sev_scale,
        text = ~paste0(country, "<br>", top_crisis),
        hovertemplate = "<b>%{text}</b><br>Crisis Severity Score: %{z:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        colorbar = cbar("Crisis<br>Severity<br>Score"),
        marker = list(line = list(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 0.4))) |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", font = chart_font, dragmode = FALSE,
         geo = list(bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", showframe = FALSE,
                    projection = list(type = "orthographic",
                                      rotation = list(lon = 20, lat = 10)),
                    showocean = TRUE, oceancolor = ocean_blue,
                    showlakes = TRUE, lakecolor = ocean_blue,
                    showrivers = TRUE, rivercolor = ocean_blue, riverwidth = 0.5,
                    showland = TRUE, landcolor = nodata_grey,
                    showcountries = TRUE, countrycolor = "#FFFFFF",
                    showcoastlines = TRUE, coastlinecolor = "#FFFFFF", coastlinewidth = 1,
                    lonaxis = list(showgrid = TRUE, gridcolor = grid_blue),
                    lataxis = list(showgrid = TRUE, gridcolor = grid_blue)),
         margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 0, b = 0),
         annotations = list(nodata_key("No crisis recorded"))) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, scrollZoom = FALSE) |>
  htmlwidgets::onRender("
    function(el) {
      var lon = 20, paused = false, mode = 'globe';
      var reduceMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

      // Pause while the mouse is over the map (or briefly after a tap)
      el.addEventListener('mouseenter', function() { paused = true; });
      el.addEventListener('mouseleave', function() { paused = false; });
      el.addEventListener('touchstart', function() {
        paused = true;
        setTimeout(function() { paused = false; }, 6000);
      });

      function showFlat() {
        mode = 'flat';
        Plotly.relayout(el, {
          'geo.projection.type': 'natural earth',
          'geo.projection.rotation.lon': 0,
          'geo.projection.rotation.lat': 0,
          'geo.showocean': true,
          'geo.lonaxis.showgrid': false,
          'geo.lataxis.showgrid': false
        });
      }

      function showGlobe() {
        mode = 'globe';
        Plotly.relayout(el, {
          'geo.projection.type': 'orthographic',
          'geo.projection.rotation.lon': lon,
          'geo.projection.rotation.lat': 10,
          'geo.showocean': true,
          'geo.lonaxis.showgrid': true,
          'geo.lataxis.showgrid': true
        });
      }

      // Phones and tablets: a still, flat map (no spinning, no switching)
      if (window.matchMedia('(max-width: 768px), (pointer: coarse)').matches) {
        showFlat();
        return;
      }

      // Expanded = the map fills most of the screen in both width and height
      function checkSize() {
        var expanded = el.clientWidth  > window.innerWidth  * 0.7 &&
                       el.clientHeight > window.innerHeight * 0.7;
        if (expanded && mode === 'globe') showFlat();
        if (!expanded && mode === 'flat') showGlobe();
      }

      var resizeTimer = null;
      new ResizeObserver(function() {
        clearTimeout(resizeTimer);
        resizeTimer = setTimeout(checkSize, 150);
      }).observe(el);

      // Slow turning, only in globe mode
      function spin() {
        var onScreen = el.offsetParent !== null;   // false while another tab is open
        if (mode === 'globe' && !paused && !reduceMotion && onScreen &&
            document.visibilityState === 'visible') {
          lon = lon - 0.5;
          if (lon < -180) lon += 360;
          Plotly.relayout(el, {'geo.projection.rotation.lon': lon});
        }
        setTimeout(spin, 60);
      }
      spin();
    }
  ")
```

# About

## Row

::: {.card title="About this data"}
::: {.about-text}
**What this dashboard shows.** The maps present published data from established international sources, as published, without SA Analytical scoring. They are a starting point for questions about where support may be needed, not a ranking of where funding should go. Last updated: `r date_label(Sys.Date())`.

**Funding (beta).** The Funding tab is a beta version: its media-attention comparison is SA Analytical's own analysis, is under methodological review, and may change.

**How the sector tabs work:** each tab shows a humanitarian (acute) indicator on the left and a development (structural) indicator on the right, using the sector's own established classification or measure. SA Analytical does not create its own scores for the sectors.

**Humanitarian maps:** IPC acute food insecurity (share of the analysed population in Phase 3 or above) and people in need by sector from humanitarian needs overviews (JIAF), both via the HDX Humanitarian API, using analyses published in the last two years; wasting uses WHO/UNICEF prevalence thresholds. These analyses exist only where a humanitarian assessment has been carried out, so other countries are shown in grey as "not analysed", which does not mean there are no needs. People in need are shown as a share of the total population (World Bank).

**Development maps:** prevalence of undernourishment (FAO, SDG 2.1.1); stunting (UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Joint Malnutrition Estimates, classified with WHO/UNICEF prevalence thresholds); at least basic drinking water and sanitation (WHO/UNICEF JMP); DTP3 vaccination (WHO/UNICEF estimates, against the 90% global target) and the UHC service coverage index; primary out-of-school rate (UNESCO Institute for Statistics); urban slum population (UN-Habitat, urban areas only). All via the World Bank, using the latest value within 10 years; each value's year is shown. There is no established development benchmark for protection.

**Global vulnerability map:** the left map shows ACAPS's INFORM Severity Index (0–10) for `r ref_label`, a measure of current crisis severity. The right map shows the Development & deprivation component of the INFORM Risk Index (0–10), published annually by the European Commission Joint Research Centre and drawing on the Human Development Index and the Multidimensional Poverty Index; it is shown as published, without changes. INFORM Risk `r risk_release`, © European Union, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Both scores run from 0 to 10 but are built differently, so the two maps are best compared by pattern rather than exact value.

**Climate:** ND-GAIN Country Index (University of Notre Dame). The map shows climate vulnerability; readiness to adapt and ND-GAIN's sector vulnerability scores are on the Data page.

**Get the data:** the "Get the data" link on each map opens the tables behind it, which can be downloaded as CSV or Excel files with their sources and licences. ACAPS INFORM Severity scores are shown on the maps but are not included in the downloads; they are free from [ACAPS](https://www.acaps.org/en/data).

**Funding tab:** media visibility is each country's share of global online news coverage (GDELT Project, `r ref_label`), counting all coverage of the country. "Lowest media visibility vs. severity" is exploratory, not a measure of neglect. Appeal funding coverage is reported humanitarian funding as a share of appeal requirements (OCHA Financial Tracking Service, `r format(funding_date, "%Y")` appeals, as of `r date_label(funding_date)`).

**Disclaimer:** ACAPS, the European Commission Joint Research Centre (INFORM Risk), the IPC, OCHA and HDX, the GDELT Project, the World Bank, FAO, WHO, UNICEF, UNESCO, UN-Habitat and the University of Notre Dame (ND-GAIN) are independent data providers. They are not affiliated with SA Analytical and do not endorse this dashboard. The analysis and any errors are SA Analytical's own.
